fluff.overview: The Kobold IIC is a Clan-tech redesign of the original Kobold battle armor, produced by Grumium Creations for the Rasalhague Dominion. Entering service in the early 3090s, the IIC was developed to extend the Kobold platform’s operational relevance with a fundamentally different mission profile. Reconfigured as a dedicated aerial reconnaissance platform, the IIC replaced the original’s ground-combat orientation with flight capability, enhanced stealth, and hostile-environment protection, filling a scouting niche that the Dominion’s heavier Clan battle armor could not.
fluff.capabilities: The Kobold IIC abandons the original design’s ground-combat orientation in favor of aerial reconnaissance. A VTOL movement system replaces the jump jets of the base Kobold, granting sustained flight capability that dramatically expands the suit’s operational reach as a forward observer. Improved stealth armor and an integrated ECM suite make the IIC significantly harder to detect and track than its predecessor. A light TAG designator serves as the primary mission equipment, allowing troopers to paint targets for artillery and guided munitions from concealed positions. A light machine gun provides limited self-defense capability against soft targets, while HarJel systems give the suit resilience in hostile environments including vacuum and underwater operations. The trade-off is clear: the IIC carries minimal offensive armament and relies on stealth and speed rather than firepower to survive on the battlefield.
fluff.deployment: Rasalhague Dominion garrison units organized along Inner Sphere infantry conventions employed the Kobold IIC in four-trooper squads for aerial scouting missions. Former FRR infantry traditions persisted in some Dominion formations, and these squads provided a VTOL-capable reconnaissance element that complemented heavier ground-based battle armor in mixed infantry platoons.
fluff.history: The Kobold IIC emerged from a recognition within the Rasalhague Dominion that the original design had grown redundant alongside the far superior Elemental. Rather than retire the suit entirely, Grumium Creations was tasked with finding a new role that could justify continued production. The answer was to abandon the ground-based scout concept in favor of a dedicated aerial reconnaissance platform. Equipped with a VTOL movement system, improved stealth armor, and HarJel self-repair systems, the IIC traded the original’s ground-fighting orientation for unmatched flexibility as a spotter and forward observer. The redesign entered production and saw service with Dominion garrison clusters, where its ability to operate in hostile environments and avoid detection made it a valuable complement to heavier Clan battle armor in combined-arms formations.
